decisive_spans.text: Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging demonstrated symmetric hypoautofluorescent lesions with hyperautofluorescent borders in the central macula bilaterally
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed thinning of the outer nuclear layer in the fovea

response.rationale: The vignette describes characteristic macular changes with symmetric hypoautofluorescent lesions and hyperautofluorescent borders, thinning of the outer nuclear layer in the fovea, progressive central visual impairment, and a family history, all of which strongly support Stargardt disease. Cone-rod dystrophy is a runner-up due to the progressive central visual impairment, color vision defects, and attenuated photopic responses, but the specific FAF and OCT findings are more indicative of Stargardt disease.
